shots.line: I wasn't looking for a ride, but here you are, blissful and oddly sensitive, withering a soul purveying both the dark and the light worlds I've known.
shots.seed_text: STYLE: a grey-box video game world at dusk. Flat untextured blocks for buildings, small lit yellow squares for windows, flat ground, a pink-violet sky with stars. Keep this exact flat blocky look; add no texture or realism. THIRD PERSON, like an open-world video game. The camera floats two metres behind him and a little above his shoulders. He is centred in the lower half of the frame, his whole body and the whole motorcycle visible from behind, about one third of the frame's height. The camera follows him and never passes him or looks away from him. HIM: a Black man in his thirties with close-cropped hair, wearing a matte black mock-neck long sleeve, black trousers and black boots, no helmet. HIS MOTORCYCLE: a low black motorcycle with one round white headlight and one red tail light. ACTION: He stands on the kerb with his back to us beside the parked motorcycle under one street lamp, and runs his hand along its tank.

shots.line: So I rub my aggressions into your steel coverings and hop on to amuse myself.

shots.line: Loneliness is having everything with no one to tell, being everywhere with no one to love and escape, wide-eyed and stone but alive and well, wandering with no clear end.

shots.line: I let the noise block the noise so the way I ride through the streets with the swag and eyes turn, has twists, improve, yeah, the magic still exists. All preparations to live and dream in darkness I no longer desire.

shots.line: The moon settles and the tease of distant stars subsides and I can see a morning ahead for me. It looks like a morning I could believe in, a morning where loss and life aren't so well, ripe with sunlight that's deceptively warm.

shots.line: The tripping of birds, feeling of nests, spring out of the night that has covered me, with my own curiosities for a chance at an end, where everything will be okay.
